item.title: Relay Therapeutics PI3K Inhibitor
item.description:
• Summary: Relay Therapeutics reported that its PI3Kα inhibitor (RLY-2608) achieved a 60% response rate in a Phase 2 study for vascular anomalies, a rare disease. This efficacy bar surpassed Novartis's alpelisib, positioning Relay's candidate as a potential best-in-class treatment for these blood vessel disorders.
  • MoAs: PI3Kα inhibitor – inhibits the alpha isoform of phosphoinositide 3-kinase, blocking downstream signaling pathways that promote cell growth and survival in abnormal vasculature.
  • Sources: BioSpace, BioPharma Dive, Endpoints News, Fierce Biotech

item.title: BioMarin Rare Disease Setback
item.description:
• Summary: BioMarin experienced a major setback as its investigational therapy for ENPP1 deficiency failed in a Phase 3 trial, showing no clinical benefit. This flop deals a blow to the company's rare disease portfolio, previously hit by other pipeline disappointments.
  • MoAs: Enzyme replacement therapy – provides functional ENPP1 enzyme to compensate for the genetic deficiency that leads to metabolic abnormalities.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, BioSpace, Endpoints News

item.title: Wave Life Sciences RNA Editing AATD
item.description:
• Summary: Wave Life Sciences is developing an RNA editing therapy for Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD), aiming for monthly dosing. The therapy uses a proprietary platform to correct the underlying genetic mutation in the SERPINA1 gene.
  • MoAs: RNA editing – uses an engineered guide RNA to recruit endogenous ADAR enzymes to edit specific adenosine to inosine in the target mRNA, correcting the mutation and restoring functional AAT protein production.
  • Sources: Endpoints News

item.title: AI Rare Disease Treatment Discovery
item.description:
• Summary: Artificial intelligence was used to identify a treatment for a newborn with an ultra-rare disease, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven approaches in diagnosing and developing therapies for rare conditions.
  • MoAs: N/A
